In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods and tools to support the construction of concurrent programs which have been shown to be correct with respect to a given specification.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
concurrent object-orientated programming is an attractive target for development methods based on a granularity-free notion of atomicity.
the granularity of a program's steps is not an issue which can be avoided by fixing the granularity of the atomic steps in the program.
the development method is sound, but the soundness depends crucially on the notion of atomicity used in the method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the granularity of the development process should be determined by the programmer, not by the programming language.
the granularity of a concurrent system should be determined by the granularity of the components of the system, and not vice versa.
the use of rely/guarantee conditions in a development method is a promising approach for the development of concurrent object-oriented programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
granularity can be a useful tool in the development of concurrent software.
granularity is an issue which should be addressed by the development method, rather than the programmer.
a development method based on granularity can be implemented in a language with concurrency and object-oriented programming.
